## Add ECS deployment circuit breaker support to server group creation

Implement a new boolean configuration option to enable or disable the ECS deployment circuit breaker when creating server groups. This option should default to false so existing behavior remains unchanged. The setting needs to be propagated through the server group description and applied to the ECS service deployment configuration during the create operation, with corresponding test coverage for both enabled and disabled states.

227:     if (description.getTargetGroupMappings() != null) {

235:         if (AWSVPC_NETWORK_MODE.equals(description.getNetworkMode())

357:   protected RegisterTaskDefinitionRequest makeTaskDefinitionRequestFromArtifact(
358:       String ecsServiceRole, EcsServerGroupName newServerGroupName) {
359: 
360:     RegisterTaskDefinitionRequest requestTemplate = null;
361:     if (description.isEvaluateTaskDefinitionArtifactExpressions()) {
362:       requestTemplate = getSpelProcessedArtifact();
363:     } else {
364:       requestTemplate = getArtifactFromFile();
365:     }
366: 
367:     String templateMode = requestTemplate.getNetworkMode();
368:     if (templateMode != null
369:         && !templateMode.isEmpty()
370:         && !templateMode.equals(description.getNetworkMode())) {
371:       throw new IllegalArgumentException(
372:           "Task definition networkMode does not match server group value. Found '"
373:               + templateMode
374:               + "' but expected '"
375:               + description.getNetworkMode()
376:               + "'");
377:     }
378: 
379:     List<ContainerDefinition> containers = requestTemplate.getContainerDefinitions();
380:     if (containers.size() == 0) {
381:       throw new IllegalArgumentException(
382:           "Provided task definition does not contain any container definitions.");
383:     }
384: 
385:     description
386:         .getContainerToImageMap()
387:         .forEach(
388:             (k, v) -> {
389:               // check if taskDefTemplate contains matching container
390:               List<ContainerDefinition> matches =
391:                   containers.stream()
392:                       .filter(x -> x.getName().equals(k))
393:                       .collect(Collectors.toList());
394: 
395:               if (matches.size() != 1) {
396:                 throw new IllegalArgumentException(
397:                     "Invalid number of matching containers found for mapping '"
398:                         + k
399:                         + "'. Have "
400:                         + matches.size()
401:                         + " but expected 1.");
402:               }
403: 
404:               // interpolate container mappings
405:               matches.get(0).setImage(v);
406:             });
407: 
408:     containers.forEach(
409:         (c) -> {
410:           Collection<KeyValuePair> updatedEnv =
411:               setSpinnakerEnvVars(c.getEnvironment(), newServerGroupName);
412:           c.setEnvironment(updatedEnv);
413: 
414:           Map<String, String> updatedLabels =
415:               setSpinnakerDockerLabels(c.getDockerLabels(), newServerGroupName);
416:           c.setDockerLabels(updatedLabels);
417:         });
418: 
419:     requestTemplate.setFamily(newServerGroupName.getFamilyName());
420: 
421:     if (FARGATE.equals(description.getLaunchType())) {
422:       String templateExecutionRole = requestTemplate.getExecutionRoleArn();
423: 
424:       if (templateExecutionRole == null || templateExecutionRole.isEmpty()) {
425:         requestTemplate.setExecutionRoleArn(ecsServiceRole);
426:       }
427:     } else if (description.getCapacityProviderStrategy() != null
428:         && !description.getCapacityProviderStrategy().isEmpty()) {
429:       for (CapacityProviderStrategyItem cpStrategy : description.getCapacityProviderStrategy()) {
430:         if (FARGATE.equals(cpStrategy.getCapacityProvider())
431:             || FARGATE_SPOT.equals(cpStrategy.getCapacityProvider())) {
432:           String templateExecutionRole = requestTemplate.getExecutionRoleArn();
433: 
434:           if (templateExecutionRole == null || StringUtils.isBlank(templateExecutionRole)) {
435:             requestTemplate.setExecutionRoleArn(ecsServiceRole);
436:           }
437: 
438:           return requestTemplate;
439:         }
440:       }
441:     }
442: 
443:     return requestTemplate;
444:   }

446:   private File downloadTaskDefinitionArtifact(Artifact taskDefArtifact) {
447:     File file = null;
448:     if (taskDefArtifact.getArtifactAccount() == null
449:         || taskDefArtifact.getArtifactAccount().isEmpty()
450:             && description.getTaskDefinitionArtifactAccount() != null
451:             && !description.getTaskDefinitionArtifactAccount().isEmpty()) {
452:       taskDefArtifact =
453:           taskDefArtifact.toBuilder()
454:               .artifactAccount(description.getTaskDefinitionArtifactAccount())
455:               .build();
456:     }
457:     try {
458:       InputStream artifactInput = artifactDownloader.download(taskDefArtifact);
459:       file = File.createTempFile(UUID.randomUUID().toString(), null);
460:       FileOutputStream fileOutputStream = new FileOutputStream(file);
461:       IOUtils.copy(artifactInput, fileOutputStream);
462:       fileOutputStream.close();
463:     } catch (IOException e) {
464:       if (file != null) {
465:         file.delete();
466:       }
467:       throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
468:     }
469:     return file;
470:   }

510:   protected CreateServiceRequest makeServiceRequest(
511:       String taskDefinitionArn,
512:       EcsServerGroupName newServerGroupName,
513:       Integer desiredCount,
514:       Namer<EcsResource> namer,
515:       boolean taggingEnabled) {
516:     Collection<ServiceRegistry> serviceRegistries = new LinkedList<>();
517:     if (description.getServiceDiscoveryAssociations() != null) {
518:       for (ServiceDiscoveryAssociation config : description.getServiceDiscoveryAssociations()) {
519:         ServiceRegistry registryEntry =
520:             new ServiceRegistry().withRegistryArn(config.getRegistry().getArn());
521: 
522:         if (config.getContainerPort() != null && config.getContainerPort() != 0) {
523:           registryEntry.setContainerPort(config.getContainerPort());
524: 
525:           if (StringUtils.isEmpty(config.getContainerName())) {
526:             registryEntry.setContainerName(newServerGroupName.getContainerName());
527:           } else {
528:             registryEntry.setContainerName(config.getContainerName());
529:           }
530:         }
531: 
532:         serviceRegistries.add(registryEntry);
533:       }
534:     }
535: 
536:     DeploymentConfiguration deploymentConfiguration =
537:         new DeploymentConfiguration().withMinimumHealthyPercent(100).withMaximumPercent(200);
538: 
539:     CreateServiceRequest request =
540:         new CreateServiceRequest()
541:             .withServiceName(newServerGroupName.getServiceName())
542:             .withDesiredCount(desiredCount)
543:             .withCluster(description.getEcsClusterName())
544:             .withTaskDefinition(taskDefinitionArn)
545:             .withPlacementConstraints(description.getPlacementConstraints())
546:             .withPlacementStrategy(description.getPlacementStrategySequence())
547:             .withServiceRegistries(serviceRegistries)
548:             .withDeploymentConfiguration(deploymentConfiguration)
549:             .withEnableExecuteCommand(description.isEnableExecuteCommand());
550: 
551:     List<Tag> taskDefTags = new LinkedList<>();
552:     if (description.getTags() != null && !description.getTags().isEmpty()) {
553:       for (Map.Entry<String, String> entry : description.getTags().entrySet()) {
554:         taskDefTags.add(new Tag().withKey(entry.getKey()).withValue(entry.getValue()));
555:       }
556:     }
557: 
558:     // Apply moniker strategy which may add tags
559:     namer.applyMoniker(
560:         new EcsResource() {
561:           @Override
562:           public String getName() {
563:             return request.getServiceName();
564:           }
565: 
566:           // Used by Frigga when moniker support is disabled
567:           public void setName(String name) {
568:             request.setServiceName(name);
569:           }
570: 
571:           @Override
572:           public List<Tag> getResourceTags() {
573:             return taskDefTags;
574:           }
575:         },
576:         newServerGroupName.getMoniker());
577: 
578:     // Only add tags if they're set as it's an optional feature for ECS
579:     if (taggingEnabled) {
580:       request
581:           .withTags(taskDefTags)
582:           .withEnableECSManagedTags(true)
583:           .withPropagateTags(PropagateTags.SERVICE.toString());
584:     } else {
585:       if (!taskDefTags.isEmpty()) {
586:         throw new IllegalArgumentException(
587:             "ECS account settings for account "
588:                 + description.getAccount()
589:                 + " do not allow tagging as `serviceLongArnFormat` and `taskLongArnFormat` are not enabled.");
590:       }
591:     }
592: 
593:     request.withLoadBalancers(retrieveLoadBalancers(newServerGroupName.getContainerName()));
594: 
595:     if (AWSVPC_NETWORK_MODE.equals(description.getNetworkMode())) {
596:       Collection<String> subnetIds =
597:           subnetSelector.resolveSubnetsIdsForMultipleSubnetTypes(
598:               description.getAccount(),
599:               description.getRegion(),
600:               description.getAvailabilityZones().get(description.getRegion()),
601:               getSubnetTypes());
602:       Collection<String> vpcIds =
603:           subnetSelector.getSubnetVpcIds(
604:               description.getAccount(), description.getRegion(), subnetIds);
605:       Collection<String> securityGroupIds =
606:           securityGroupSelector.resolveSecurityGroupNames(
607:               description.getAccount(),
608:               description.getRegion(),
609:               description.getSecurityGroupNames(),
610:               vpcIds);
611: 
612:       AwsVpcConfiguration awsvpcConfiguration =
613:           new AwsVpcConfiguration().withSecurityGroups(securityGroupIds).withSubnets(subnetIds);
614: 
615:       if (description.getAssociatePublicIpAddress() != null) {
616:         awsvpcConfiguration.withAssignPublicIp(
617:             description.getAssociatePublicIpAddress() ? "ENABLED" : "DISABLED");
618:       }
619: 
620:       request.withNetworkConfiguration(
621:           new NetworkConfiguration().withAwsvpcConfiguration(awsvpcConfiguration));
622:     }
623: 
624:     if (!StringUtils.isEmpty(description.getLaunchType())) {
625:       request.withLaunchType(description.getLaunchType());
626:     } else if (description.getCapacityProviderStrategy() != null
627:         && !description.getCapacityProviderStrategy().isEmpty()) {
628:       request.withCapacityProviderStrategy(description.getCapacityProviderStrategy());
629:     }
630: 
631:     if (!StringUtils.isEmpty(description.getPlatformVersion())) {

We need to update the clouddriver-kubernetes module to be compatible with the Kubernetes Java client v13 (brought in by the Spring Boot 2.6.x / Spring Cloud 2021.0.8 upgrade). The v13 client has significant API changes from v11 that break our current code:

1. **Fluent builder classes moved**: The client-java v13 release moved builder patterns (e.g., `V1ContainerBuilder`, `V1DeploymentBuilder`, `V1ReplicaSetBuilder`, `V1HorizontalPodAutoscalerBuilder`) into a separate `client-java-api-fluent` module. Tests that reference these builders fail to compile because the dependency isn't on the classpath.

2. **Joda-Time replaced with java.time**: The v13 client switched from `org.joda.time.DateTime` to `java.time.OffsetDateTime` for timestamp fields. Our code in `KubernetesJobProvider` and `KubernetesJobStatus` still uses Joda-Time types, causing compilation errors.

3. **API change for timestamps**: `V1ObjectMeta.getCreationTimestamp()` now returns `OffsetDateTime` instead of `DateTime`. The `getMillis()` method no longer exists.

The goal is to:
- Add the `client-java-api-fluent` dependency (v13.0.2) to the kubernetes and web modules where needed
- Migrate all Joda-Time `DateTime` usage to `java.time.OffsetDateTime` in our Kubernetes code
- Update timestamp handling to convert `OffsetDateTime` to epoch milliseconds properly

This is a focused compatibility fix — please do not refactor unrelated code or explore broader migration opportunities.

## Environment Setup
Check these files for build and test setup:
    - `build.gradle` (root) — main Gradle configuration
    - `settings.gradle` — module definitions
    - `clouddriver-kubernetes/clouddriver-kubernetes.gradle` — kubernetes module dependencies and test configuration
    - `clouddriver-web/clouddriver-web.gradle` — web module dependencies
    - `gradle.properties` — version properties
    - `.github/workflows/build.yml` — CI build process

## Implementation Plan
1. **Add fluent dependency to kubernetes module**: In `clouddriver-kubernetes/clouddriver-kubernetes.gradle`, add `implementation "io.kubernetes:client-java-api-fluent:13.0.2"` alongside the existing `implementation "io.kubernetes:client-java"` line.

    2. **Replace dependency in web module**: In `clouddriver-web/clouddriver-web.gradle`, change `testImplementation "io.kubernetes:client-java"` to `testImplementation "io.kubernetes:client-java-api-fluent:13.0.2"` since the test only needs the fluent builders.

    3. **Fix timestamp conversion in KubernetesJobStatus**: In `clouddriver-kubernetes/src/main/java/com/netflix/spinnaker/clouddriver/kubernetes/model/KubernetesJobStatus.java`, change `this.createdTime = job.getMetadata().getCreationTimestamp().getMillis();` to use the new API: `this.createdTime = job.getMetadata().getCreationTimestamp().toInstant().toEpochMilli();`

    4. **Update imports in KubernetesJobProvider**: In `clouddriver-kubernetes/src/main/java/com/netflix/spinnaker/clouddriver/kubernetes/provider/view/KubernetesJobProvider.java`, replace `import org.joda.time.DateTime;` with `import java.time.OffsetDateTime;`

    5. **Update sorting logic in KubernetesJobProvider**: Change the pod sorting comparator to use `OffsetDateTime`:
       - Replace `DateTime dtDefault = new DateTime(0);` with `OffsetDateTime dtDefault = OffsetDateTime.now();` (or a suitable epoch-based default)
       - Change types `DateTime time1`/`DateTime time2` to `OffsetDateTime`
       - The `compareTo` method works the same for both types

    6. **Update test in ObjectMapperTest**: In `clouddriver-web/src/test/java/com/netflix/spinnaker/clouddriver/config/ObjectMapperTest.java`, replace `import org.joda.time.DateTime;` with `import java.time.OffsetDateTime;`, and change `DateTime.now()` calls to `OffsetDateTime.now()`.

    7. **Verify kubernetes tests compile**: The explicit fluent dependency should resolve the missing builder class imports in test files like `ArtifactReplacerTest`.

Currently clouddriver installation only provides a single kubectl binary (version 1.22.17). This makes it impossible to support clusters running different Kubernetes versions, since newer Kubernetes clusters may require a newer kubectl version to function correctly.

    Implement support for installing multiple kubectl versions during image/package build, allowing users to configure which kubectl binary to use per Kubernetes account via a `kubectlExecutable` field in the cluster config. The versions should be stored without patch version in the binary name (e.g., `kubectl-1.28`), so that patch updates can be made without requiring configuration changes. A symlink `kubectl` should be maintained to the default version to preserve backwards compatibility with existing configurations.

    Additionally, update the integration test infrastructure to test against multiple kubectl versions, ensuring the fix works across the supported Kubernetes cluster image matrix.

## Environment Setup
Check these repo files for build/install/test instructions:
    - `build.gradle` and `clouddriver-kubernetes/clouddriver-kubernetes.gradle` for Gradle build and test configuration
    - `.github/workflows/integration-tests-kubernetes.yml` for CI integration test setup
    - `Dockerfile.java11.slim`, `Dockerfile.java11.ubuntu`, `Dockerfile.slim`, `Dockerfile.ubuntu` for image build configuration

    3. **Update integration test Gradle configuration** (`clouddriver-kubernetes/clouddriver-kubernetes.gradle`):

161:         ReadableByteChannel rbc = Channels.newChannel(is);
162:         FileOutputStream fos = new FileOutputStream(binary.toFile())) {
163:       fos.getChannel().transferFrom(rbc, 0, Long.MAX_VALUE);
164:       fos.flush();
165:       assertThat(binary.toFile().setExecutable(true, false)).isEqualTo(true);

332:   private static String parseLink(retrofit.client.Header header) {
333:     if (!header.name.equalsIgnoreCase("link")) {
334:       return null
335:     }
336: 
337:     def links = header.value.split(";").collect { it.trim() }
338: 
339:     if (!(links.findAll { String tok ->
340:       tok.replace(" ", "").equalsIgnoreCase("rel=\"next\"")
341:     })) {
342:       return null
343:     }
344: 
345:     def path = links.find { String tok ->
346:       tok && tok.getAt(0) == "<" && tok.getAt(tok.length() - 1) == ">"
347:     }
348: 
349:     def link = path?.substring(1, path.length() - 1)
350: 
351:     try {
352:       def url = new URL(link)
353:       link = url.getFile().substring(1)
354:     } catch (Exception e) {
355:       // In the case where the link isn't a valid URL, we were passed just the
356:       // relative path[1]
357:       // [1] https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986#section-5
358:     }
359: 
360:     return link.startsWith('/') ? link.replaceFirst('/', '') : link
361:   }

363:   private static String findNextLink(List<retrofit.client.Header> headers) {
364:     if (!headers) {
365:       return null
366:     }
367: 
368:     def paths = headers.collect { header ->
369:       parseLink(header)
370:     }.findAll { it }
371: 
372:     // We are at the end of the pagination.
373:     if (!paths || paths.size() == 0) {
374:       return null
375:     } else if (paths.size() > 1) {
376:       throw new DockerRegistryOperationException("Ambiguous number of Link headers provided, the following paths were identified: $paths")
377:     }
378: 
379:     return paths[0]
380:   }

386:   public DockerRegistryCatalog getCatalog(String path = null) {
387:     if (catalogFile) {
388:       log.info("Using catalog list at $catalogFile")
389:       try {
390:         String userDefinedCatalog = new File(catalogFile).getText()
391:         return (DockerRegistryCatalog) new Gson().fromJson(userDefinedCatalog, DockerRegistryCatalog.class)
392:       } catch (Exception e) {
393:         throw new DockerRegistryOperationException("Unable to read catalog file $catalogFile: " + e.getMessage(), e)
394:       }
395:     }
396: 
397:     def response
398:     try {
399:       response = request({
400:         path ? registryService.get(path, tokenService.basicAuthHeader, userAgent) :
401:           registryService.getCatalog(paginateSize, tokenService.basicAuthHeader, userAgent)
402:       }, { token ->
403:         path ? registryService.get(path, token, userAgent) :
404:           registryService.getCatalog(paginateSize, token, userAgent)
405:       }, "_catalog")
406:     } catch (Exception e) {
407:       log.warn("Error encountered during catalog of $path", e)
408:       return new DockerRegistryCatalog(repositories: [])
409:     }
410: 
411:     def nextPath = findNextLink(response?.headers)
412:     def catalog = (DockerRegistryCatalog) converter.fromBody(response.body, DockerRegistryCatalog)
413: 
414:     if(repositoriesRegex) {
415:       catalog.repositories = catalog.repositories.findAll { it ==~ repositoriesRegex }
416:     }
417:     if (nextPath) {
418:       def nextCatalog = getCatalog(nextPath)
419:       catalog.repositories.addAll(nextCatalog.repositories)
420:     }
421: 
422:     return catalog
423:   }

451:       doCheckV2Availability()

453:       // If no credentials are supplied, and we got a 401, the best[1] we can do is assume the registry is OK.

455:       if (!tokenService.basicAuthHeader && error instanceof SpinnakerHttpException && ((SpinnakerHttpException)error).getResponseCode() == 401) {

457:       }

476:   /*
477:    * Implements token request flow described here https://docs.docker.com/registry/spec/auth/token/
478:    * The tokenService also caches tokens for us, so it will attempt to use an old token before retrying.
479:    */
480:   public Response request(Closure<Response> withoutToken, Closure<Response> withToken, String target) {
481:     try {
482:       DockerBearerToken dockerToken = tokenService.getToken(target)
483:       String token
484:       if (dockerToken) {
485:         token = "Bearer ${(dockerToken.bearer_token ?: dockerToken.token) ?: dockerToken.access_token}"
486:       }
487: 
488:       Response response
489:       try {
490:         if (token) {
491:           response = withToken(token)
492:         } else {
493:           response = withoutToken()
494:         }
495:       } catch (SpinnakerHttpException error) {
496:         def status = error.getResponseCode()
497:         // note, this is a workaround for registries that should be returning
498:         // 401 when a token expires
499:         if ([400, 401].contains(status)) {
500:           String authenticateHeader = null
501: 
502:           error.headers.entrySet().forEach { header ->
503:             if (header.key.equalsIgnoreCase("www-authenticate")) {
504:               authenticateHeader = header.value
505:             }
506:           }
507: 
508:           if (!authenticateHeader) {
509:             log.warn "Registry $address returned status $status for request '$target' without a WWW-Authenticate header"
510:             tokenService.clearToken(target)
511:             throw error
512:           }
513: 
514:           String bearerPrefix = "bearer "
515:           String basicPrefix = "basic "
516:           if (bearerPrefix.equalsIgnoreCase(authenticateHeader.substring(0, bearerPrefix.length()))) {
517:             // If we got a 401 and the request requires bearer auth, get a new token and try again
518:             dockerToken = tokenService.getToken(target, authenticateHeader.substring(bearerPrefix.length()))
519:             token = "Bearer ${(dockerToken.bearer_token ?: dockerToken.token) ?: dockerToken.access_token}"
520:             response = withToken(token)
521:           } else if (basicPrefix.equalsIgnoreCase(authenticateHeader.substring(0, basicPrefix.length()))) {
522:             // If we got a 401 and the request requires basic auth, there's no point in trying again
523:             tokenService.clearToken(target)
524:             throw error
525:           } else {
526:             tokenService.clearToken(target)
527:             throw new DockerRegistryAuthenticationException("Docker registry must support 'Bearer' or 'Basic' authentication.")
528:           }
529:         } else {
530:           throw error
531:         }
532:       }
533: 
534:       return response
535:     } catch (DockerRegistryAuthenticationException e) {
536:       log.error "Error authenticating with registry $address, for request '$target': ${e.getMessage()}"
537:       throw e
538:     }

41:       Registry registry,

43:       SecurityConfig.OperationsSecurityConfigurationProperties opsSecurityConfigProps,
44:       AccountDefinitionSecretManager secretManager) {
45:     this.registry = registry;
46:     this.fiatPermissionEvaluator = fiatPermissionEvaluator.orElse(null);
47:     this.opsSecurityConfigProps = opsSecurityConfigProps;
48:     this.secretManager = secretManager;
49: 
50:     this.skipAuthorizationId = registry.createId("authorization.skipped");
51:     this.missingApplicationId = registry.createId("authorization.missingApplication");
52:     this.authorizationId = registry.createId("authorization");
53:   }
54: 
55:   public void authorize(Object description, Errors errors) {
56:     authorize(description, errors, List.of(ResourceType.ACCOUNT, ResourceType.APPLICATION));
57:   }
58: 
59:   public void authorize(Object description, Errors errors, Collection<ResourceType> resourceTypes) {
60:     if (fiatPermissionEvaluator == null || description == null) {
61:       return;
62:     }
63: 
64:     Authentication auth = SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication();
65: 
66:     String account = null;
67:     List<String> applications = new ArrayList<>();
68:     boolean requiresApplicationRestriction = true;
69: 
70:     if (description instanceof AccountNameable) {
71:       AccountNameable accountNameable = (AccountNameable) description;
72: 
73:       requiresApplicationRestriction = accountNameable.requiresApplicationRestriction();
74: 
75:       if (!accountNameable.requiresAuthorization(opsSecurityConfigProps)) {
76:         registry
77:             .counter(
78:                 skipAuthorizationId.withTag(
79:                     "descriptionClass", description.getClass().getSimpleName()))
80:             .increment();
81: 
82:         log.info(
83:             "Skipping authorization for operation `{}` in account `{}`.",
84:             description.getClass().getSimpleName(),
85:             accountNameable.getAccount());
86:       } else {
87:         account = accountNameable.getAccount();
88:       }
89:     }
90: 
91:     if (description instanceof ApplicationNameable) {
92:       ApplicationNameable applicationNameable = (ApplicationNameable) description;
93:       applications.addAll(
94:           Optional.ofNullable(applicationNameable.getApplications())
95:               .orElse(Collections.emptyList())
96:               .stream()
97:               .filter(Objects::nonNull)
98:               .collect(Collectors.toList()));
99:     }
100: 
101:     if (description instanceof ResourcesNameable) {
102:       ResourcesNameable resourcesNameable = (ResourcesNameable) description;
103: 
104:       applications.addAll(
105:           Optional.ofNullable(resourcesNameable.getResourceApplications())
106:               .orElse(Collections.emptyList())
107:               .stream()
108:               .filter(Objects::nonNull)
109:               .collect(Collectors.toList()));
110:     }
111: 
112:     boolean hasPermission = true;
113:     if (resourceTypes.contains(ResourceType.ACCOUNT)
114:         && account != null
115:         && !secretManager.canAccessAccountWithSecrets(auth.getName(), account)) {
116:       hasPermission = false;
117:       errors.reject("authorization.account", format("Access denied to account %s", account));
118:     }
119: 
120:     if (resourceTypes.contains(ResourceType.APPLICATION) && !applications.isEmpty()) {
121:       fiatPermissionEvaluator.storeWholePermission();
122: 
123:       for (String application : applications) {
124:         if (!fiatPermissionEvaluator.hasPermission(auth, application, "APPLICATION", "WRITE")) {
125:           hasPermission = false;
126:           errors.reject(
127:               "authorization.application", format("Access denied to application %s", application));
128:         }
129:       }
130:     }
131: 
132:     if (requiresApplicationRestriction && account != null && applications.isEmpty()) {
133:       registry
134:           .counter(
135:               missingApplicationId
136:                   .withTag("descriptionClass", description.getClass().getSimpleName())
137:                   .withTag("hasValidationErrors", errors.hasErrors()))
138:           .increment();
139: 
140:       log.warn(
141:           "No application(s) specified for operation with account restriction (type: {}, account: {}, hasValidationErrors: {})",
142:           description.getClass().getSimpleName(),
143:           account,
144:           errors.hasErrors());
145:     }
146: 
147:     registry
148:         .counter(
149:             authorizationId
150:                 .withTag("descriptionClass", description.getClass().getSimpleName())
151:                 .withTag("success", hasPermission))
152:         .increment();
153:   }
154: }

40: /**

44: @Beta
45: @NonnullByDefault
46: @RequiredArgsConstructor

49:   private final AccountDefinitionSecretManager secretManager;
50:   private final AccountCredentialsProvider accountCredentialsProvider;
51:   private final AccountSecurityPolicy policy;

54:   /**
55:    * Lists accounts by type that the current user has {@link Authorization#WRITE} access. Users who
56:    * only have {@link Authorization#READ} access can only view related items like load balancers,
57:    * clusters, security groups, etc., that use the account, but they may not directly use or view
58:    * account definitions and credentials.
59:    *
60:    * @see AccountDefinitionRepository#listByType(String, int, String)
61:    */
62:   @PreAuthorize("@accountSecurity.isAccountManager(authentication.name)")
63:   @PostFilter(
64:       "@accountDefinitionSecretManager.canAccessAccountWithSecrets(authentication.name, filterObject.name)")
65:   public List<? extends CredentialsDefinition> listAccountDefinitionsByType(
66:       String accountType, int limit, @Nullable String startingAccountName) {
67:     return repository.listByType(accountType, limit, startingAccountName);
68:   }

70:   @PreAuthorize("@accountSecurity.isAccountManager(authentication.name)")
71:   public CredentialsDefinition createAccount(CredentialsDefinition definition) {
72:     String name = definition.getName();
73:     String username = AuthenticatedRequest.getSpinnakerUser().orElse("anonymous");
74:     if (accountCredentialsProvider.getCredentials(name) != null) {
75:       throw new InvalidRequestException(
76:           String.format("Cannot create an account which already exists (name: %s)", name));
77:     }
78:     validateAccountWritePermissions(username, definition, AccountAction.CREATE);
79:     repository.create(definition);
80:     return definition;
81:   }

84:   public CredentialsDefinition saveAccount(CredentialsDefinition definition) {
85:     String name = definition.getName();
86:     String username = AuthenticatedRequest.getSpinnakerUser().orElse("anonymous");
87:     if (accountCredentialsProvider.getCredentials(name) != null
88:         && !policy.canModifyAccount(username, name)) {
89:       throw new AccessDeniedException(
90:           String.format("Unauthorized to overwrite existing account (name: %s)", name));
91:     }
92:     validateAccountWritePermissions(username, definition, AccountAction.SAVE);
93:     repository.save(definition);
94:     return definition;
95:   }

98:   public CredentialsDefinition updateAccount(CredentialsDefinition definition) {

101:       throw new InvalidRequestException(
102:           String.format("Cannot update an account which does not exist (name: %s)", name));
103:     }
104:     String username = AuthenticatedRequest.getSpinnakerUser().orElse("anonymous");
105:     validateAccountWritePermissions(username, definition, AccountAction.UPDATE);
106:     repository.update(definition);
107:     return definition;
108:   }

110:   @PreAuthorize("@accountSecurity.canModifyAccount(authentication.name, #accountName)")
111:   public void deleteAccount(String accountName) {
112:     repository.delete(accountName);
113:   }

115:   /**
116:    * Deletes an account by name if the current user has {@link Authorization#WRITE} access to the
117:    * given account.
118:    */

120:   public List<AccountDefinitionRepository.Revision> getAccountHistory(String accountName) {
121:     return repository.revisionHistory(accountName);
122:   }

124:   private void validateAccountWritePermissions(
125:       String username, CredentialsDefinition definition, AccountAction action) {
126:     if (policy.isAdmin(username)) {
127:       return;
128:     }
129:     var accountName = definition.getName();
130:     var type = definition.getClass();
131:     Set<String> authorizedRoles =
132:         extractors.stream()
133:             .filter(extractor -> extractor.supportsType(type))
134:             .flatMap(extractor -> extractor.getAuthorizedRoles(definition).stream())
135:             .collect(Collectors.toSet());
136:     var userRoles = policy.getRoles(username);
137:     // if the account defines authorized roles and the user has no roles in common with these
138:     // authorized roles, then the user attempted to create an account they'd immediately be
139:     // locked out from which is a poor user experience
140:     // (Collections::disjoint returns true if both collections have no elements in common)
141:     if (!authorizedRoles.isEmpty() && Collections.disjoint(userRoles, authorizedRoles)) {
142:       throw new InvalidRequestException(
143:           String.format(
144:               "Cannot %s account without granting permissions for current user (name: %s)",
145:               action.name().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT), accountName));
146:     }
147:     Set<UserSecretReference> secretReferences = new HashSet<>();
148:     ReflectionUtils.doWithFields(
149:         type,
150:         field ->
151:             UserSecretReference.tryParse(field.get(definition)).ifPresent(secretReferences::add),
152:         field -> field.getType() == String.class);
153:     // if the account uses any UserSecrets and the user has no roles in common with any of
154:     // the UserSecrets, then don't allow the user to save this account due to lack of authorization
155:     for (var ref : secretReferences) {
156:       try {
157:         var secret = secretManager.getUserSecret(ref);
158:         var secretRoles = Set.copyOf(secret.getRoles());
159:         // (Collections::disjoint returns true if both collections have no elements in common)
160:         if (Collections.disjoint(userRoles, secretRoles)) {
161:           throw new AccessDeniedException(
162:               String.format(
163:                   "Unauthorized to %s account with user secret %s",
164:                   action.name().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT), ref));
165:         }
166:       } catch (SecretException e) {
167:         throw new InvalidRequestException(e);
168:       }
169:     }
170:   }
171: 
172:   private enum AccountAction {
173:     CREATE,
174:     UPDATE,
175:     SAVE
176:   }
177: }

32: @RequiredArgsConstructor
33: @NonnullByDefault
34: public class AccountDefinitionSecretManager {
35:   @Delegate private final UserSecretManager userSecretManager;
36:   private final AccountSecurityPolicy policy;
37: 
38:   private final Map<String, Set<UserSecretReference>> refsByAccountName = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
39: 
40:   /**
41:    * Gets a user secret string value for the given account. User secret references are tracked
42:    * through this method to support time-of-use access control checks for accounts after they've
43:    * been loaded by the system.
44:    *
45:    * @param reference parsed user secret reference to decrypt
46:    * @param accountName name of account requesting the user secret
47:    * @return the contents of the requested user secret string
48:    */
49:   public String getUserSecretString(UserSecretReference reference, String accountName) {
50:     var secret = getUserSecret(reference);
51:     refsByAccountName
52:         .computeIfAbsent(accountName, ignored -> ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet())
53:         .add(reference);
54:     var parameterName = StandardSecretParameter.KEY.getParameterName();
55:     var secretKey = reference.getParameters().getOrDefault(parameterName, "");
56:     try {
57:       return secret.getSecretString(secretKey);
58:     } catch (NoSuchElementException e) {
59:       throw new SecretDecryptionException(e);
60:     }
61:   }
62: 
63:   /**
64:    * Indicates if the given username is authorized to access the given account. When Fiat is
65:    * enabled, this allows admins to access accounts along with users who have both WRITE permission
66:    * on the account and are authorized to use any provided {@link UserSecretReference} data.
67:    *
68:    * @param username username to check for authorization to use the given account
69:    * @param accountName the name of the account to check access to
70:    * @return true if the given username is allowed to access the given account
71:    */
72:   public boolean canAccessAccountWithSecrets(String username, String accountName) {
73:     return policy.isAdmin(username)
74:         || !accountDefinitionUsesUnauthorizedUserSecrets(username, accountName)
75:             && policy.canUseAccount(username, accountName);
76:   }
77: 
78:   /**
79:    * Checks the account definition for the provided account name and returns true if said account
80:    * references at least one UserSecret for which the provided user does not have a role in common
81:    * with. If the account definition uses no UserSecrets or the provided user is allowed to use all
82:    * the UserSecrets referenced, then this returns false.
83:    */
84:   private boolean accountDefinitionUsesUnauthorizedUserSecrets(
85:       String username, String accountName) {
86:     var userRoles = policy.getRoles(username);
87:     // if at least one UserSecret is referenced which the user has no common roles with
88:     return refsByAccountName.getOrDefault(accountName, Set.of()).stream()
89:         .map(this::getUserSecret)
90:         .anyMatch(secret -> Collections.disjoint(secret.getRoles(), userRoles));
91:     // Collections::disjoint checks if both collections have nothing in common (i.e., an empty set
92:     // intersection)
93:   }
